findings.title: Fail closed when the installation webhook has not created an Integration
findings.body: When no Integration exists for the supplied installation_id, this branch advances the pipeline without comparing the authenticated GitHub user with the installer. build_integration then retrieves the installation using app credentials, which does not establish that the authenticated user owns it. A caller can therefore link someone else's installation if its webhook has not yet been processed (or was not delivered). Require trusted installer information and validate it before advancing, including in this branch.

findings.title: Handle integrations without sender metadata
findings.body: The new check unconditionally indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"], but build_integration only saves sender when it is present in pipeline state. The normal setup flow in the tests explicitly creates metadata without sender. If such an Integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed, attempting to link it again now raises KeyError and returns a server error instead of a controlled installation failure. Handle missing installer metadata explicitly and obtain trusted information or fail closed.

findings.title: Compare immutable GitHub user IDs rather than logins
findings.body: The ownership check compares the current OAuth login with the login stored in the installation webhook. GitHub usernames can change and old usernames can be claimed by another account. Consequently, the original installer can be rejected after renaming, while a different account that acquires the old username can pass this check for an unlinked installation. Store and compare the GitHub numeric user ID returned by /user with the webhook sender's ID instead.
